headline_fact: In Bali, sharing water can also mean sharing responsibility.
summary: Water crosses a rice terrace, then continues toward another field. Its path connects neighbours who need the same resource. In Bali, this practical dependence also connects with community organisation and ritual life.
did_you_know: In Bali, sharing water can also mean sharing responsibility.
history: Balinese traditions develop through local histories and exchanges with the wider region. Religious ideas from India meet existing ways of understanding the landscape, rather than replacing every local practice.
core_mechanics: A field depends on water that also serves other fields. Rules and cooperation help people manage this shared dependence.
why_it_matters: An introductory portrait of Balinese Hindu community life, with examples from farming villages and performance traditions.

in_depth_breakdown.real_world_application: A field depends on water that also serves other fields. Rules and cooperation help people manage this shared dependence.

impact_on_india: Bali makes the difference between cultural exchange and cultural sameness especially useful to understand.

learning_takeaways: Place and practical work help explain cultural institutions.

identity.name: Balinese culture
identity.scope: An introductory portrait of Balinese Hindu community life, with examples from farming villages and performance traditions.

culture_lesson.hook: In Bali, sharing water can also mean sharing responsibility.

opening.heading: What can an irrigation canal tell you about a culture?
opening.scene: Water crosses a rice terrace, then continues toward another field. Its path connects neighbours who need the same resource. In Bali, this practical dependence also connects with community organisation and ritual life.
opening.question: How can a shared landscape become part of a shared way of life?

origins.heartland: A volcanic island between Java and Lombok
origins.climate_and_terrain: Bali combines volcanic highlands with a tropical climate. Cultivation links upland water sources with fields farther downhill.
origins.adaptation: Terraced rice landscapes make this relationship visible. Farmers need arrangements for managing water across neighbouring fields, rather than treating each field as an isolated plot.
origins.historical_origins: Balinese traditions develop through local histories and exchanges with the wider region. Religious ideas from India meet existing ways of understanding the landscape, rather than replacing every local practice.
origins.time_context: The water-temple landscape develops over centuries; present-day communities continue to change.

milestones.event: Water temples become part of the organisation of irrigated landscapes.
milestones.significance: A physical resource and a community institution become closely connected.

daily_life.introduction: Work, community responsibilities and ritual are useful entry points into daily life. The comparison below describes particular settings rather than one lifestyle shared by everyone.

comparisons.then: Farmers organise water use through local institutions and shared responsibilities.
comparisons.now: Cultivation continues alongside pressures from development and changing livelihoods.
comparisons.why_changed: Land use and sources of income change around the farming landscape.
comparisons.who_and_where: This example concerns subak communities, rather than every resident of Bali.

comparisons.then: Practical knowledge passes through learning instruments and rehearsing with others.
comparisons.now: Transmission also involves educational and cultural institutions.
comparisons.why_changed: Formal teaching creates additional places to learn.
comparisons.who_and_where: The setting and repertoire differ between ensembles.

comparisons.then: Shared preparation and familiar dishes help mark gatherings.
comparisons.now: Food traditions also appear in household businesses and restaurants.
comparisons.why_changed: New markets create additional settings for familiar foods.
comparisons.who_and_where: Recipes and the role of a dish differ between households and occasions.

worldview.introduction: A cultural idea becomes clearer when you connect it to something people do.

concepts.meaning: This concept relates spiritual life, relationships between people, and the natural world.
concepts.everyday_example: Water-temple landscapes connect environmental management with collective and ritual responsibilities.
concepts.scope: It is a framework for understanding particular practices, not a description of every individual belief.

etiquette.situation: Entering a place used for worship
etiquette.practice: Ask the local hosts how a visitor should dress and behave.
etiquette.reason: A temple is a working community space, not only a visual attraction.
etiquette.context: Follow the guidance for that place and occasion.

markers.name: Ceremonial clothing
markers.description: Kebaya and wrapped cloth are among the forms of dress associated with ceremonial life. The occasion helps explain why clothing differs from everyday work clothes.
markers.meaning: Dress signals participation in a particular social setting.
markers.experience: Look at the whole outfit and its occasion, rather than treating one garment as a uniform.
markers.today: Ceremonial clothing remains part of contemporary public and community life.

markers.name: Water temples
markers.description: Temples stand within a wider landscape of fields and water channels. Their significance becomes clearer when you see how people use the surrounding land.
markers.meaning: Built spaces connect ritual with the management of shared resources.
markers.experience: Follow the relationship between the water source, the channel and the fields.
markers.today: These places remain part of living landscapes.

markers.name: Lawar
markers.description: Lawar combines chopped ingredients with coconut and seasonings. Different preparations use different ingredients and serve different settings.
markers.meaning: A familiar dish can link the work of preparing food with an occasion.
markers.experience: Ask what the preparation contains and when people usually serve it.
markers.today: The dish appears in local food businesses as well as ceremonial settings.

markers.name: Gamelan
markers.place_or_community: Balinese ensembles within Indonesian musical traditions
markers.description: Gamelan names an ensemble and its instruments. Percussion instruments create parts that work together rather than functioning as unrelated solo performances.
markers.meaning: Learning and playing connect musical knowledge with group participation.
markers.experience: Listen for how the different parts fit together.
markers.today: Community groups and educational institutions continue the practice.

markers.name: Galungan
markers.description: Galungan is associated with ancestors and the relationship between dharma and adharma. It places a major occasion within the rhythm of community life.
markers.meaning: Celebration gives shared ideas a place in the calendar.
markers.experience: Learn what the event means to the community before treating it as a performance.
markers.today: Families and communities maintain the occasion in contemporary life.

india_connections.introduction: Bali makes the difference between cultural exchange and cultural sameness especially useful to understand.

connections.title: Indian religious ideas in a Balinese setting
connections.explanation: The water-temple landscape reflects exchanges involving Hindu and Buddhist traditions alongside local cosmology.
connections.indian_example: Readers familiar with Hindu traditions can recognise some ideas while learning how the Balinese setting changes their expression.
connections.distinction: Shared references do not make Balinese ritual life identical to any one Indian tradition.

why_custom.title: Why sharing water becomes a community task
why_custom.custom: Cooperative water management in a terraced landscape

drivers.effect: Water moves across a landscape rather than remaining within one household’s boundary.
Local institutions give people a way to organise the shared resource.

why_custom.what_it_explains: This relationship helps explain why fields, channels and community institutions belong in the same story.

spread.introduction: Cultural influence can move through teaching, travel and performance. Movement also changes the setting in which a practice is understood.

pathways.route: Gamelan is taught and performed in settings beyond its original local communities.
pathways.what_changed: A rehearsal or concert can have a different purpose from a local ritual setting.
pathways.what_continues: Musicians continue to learn the relationships between ensemble parts.

influences.name: Ensemble learning
influences.example: Learners meet an approach in which the parts fit into a larger musical whole.
influences.connection: The practice travels through instruments, teachers and participation, not only through recordings.

living_culture.introduction: The examples in this portrait are entry points. They describe practices and settings rather than a single way to be Balinese.

variations.difference: An irrigation collective and a musical ensemble organise different activities.
variations.explanation: Both belong in a cultural portrait, but neither describes every household or profession.

key_terms.meaning: A cooperative institution connected with irrigation in Bali.

knowledge_checks.question: Why does a rice terrace belong in a cultural portrait?
knowledge_checks.answer: The field connects with institutions and shared responsibilities.
knowledge_checks.explanation: A cultural explanation looks at the relationship between practical work, ideas and community organisation.
